title: Rush Loading Carried by a Catering Order Accepted Inside the Standard Notice
content:
## The rule

Whether a catering order under a Corporate Catering Service Agreement carries a rush percentage, and how much of the printed percentage it carries, turns on two things: whether the order was accepted inside the standard lead time printed against the catering service level, and how many deliveries the agreement carried in the 6 months ending on the day the invoice is raised.

The notice the order was accepted on is counted in whole days from the day the order was placed to the service day, taken at 24 hours to the day.

1. Where the order was accepted inside the standard lead time printed against the catering service level and the agreement carried 3 or more deliveries in the 6 months ending on the day the invoice is raised, the order carries half — that is 0.5, or 50 per cent — of the rush percentage printed against that service level.
2. Where the order was accepted inside the standard lead time printed against the catering service level and the agreement carried fewer than 3 deliveries in those 6 months, the order carries the whole rush percentage printed against that service level.
3. Otherwise, the order carries no rush percentage.

## Cases

On a hypothetical Corporate Catering Service Agreement whose service level is printed with a standard lead time of 48 hours and a rush percentage of 15.0 per cent:

- an order placed 2 days before the service day holds 48 hours of notice, which is not inside the standard lead time, and carries no rush percentage, whatever the delivery record;
- an order placed 1 day before the service day holds 24 hours of notice, which is inside the standard lead time; on an agreement carrying 4 deliveries in those 6 months the percentage is 7.5 per cent, and on an agreement carrying 2 deliveries it is 15.0 per cent;
- an agreement carrying exactly 3 deliveries in those 6 months is on the first branch, since 3 or more deliveries are asked for, and the percentage is 7.5 per cent.

The delivery count is taken from the delivery entries standing in that agreement's order history over the 6 months ending on the day the invoice is raised.
